ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, officers, shareholders, UBOs, and authorized signatories against Canadian Global Affairs Canada sanctions lists, the Special Economic Measures Act and United Nations Act sanctions lists, OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons (SDN) list, UN Security Council consolidated list, UK Office of Financial Sanctions Implementation (OFSI) list, and EU consolidated sanctions list. Mandatory PEP status determination in accordance with FINTRAC guidance and PCMLTFA Regulations; enhanced due diligence is required for any individual found to be a PEP, a family member, or a close associate of a PEP, and where the risk assessment indicates higher money laundering or terrorist financing risk. Continuous sanctions list monitoring, OFAC 50% ownership rule screening, and documented risk assessments retained for a minimum of five years.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Alberta Corporate Registry (administered by the Registrar of Corporations, Service Alberta; filings submitted through authorized Alberta Registry Agents or the Corporate Registry online services)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must be expressed in English or French using Latin characters, numerals, and permitted acronyms. A mandatory legal element is required: 'Inc.', 'Corp.', 'Ltd.', 'Incorporated', 'Limited', or a prescribed French equivalent. Non-Latin script names must be transliterated phonetically into Latin characters and must remain distinguishable from existing names. The name must not be confusingly similar to any existing corporate name, trademark, or registered business name in Alberta, and must comply with the Alberta Business Corporations Act, RSA 2000, c B-9, s. 10, and the Name Regulations thereunder.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Where a proposed corporate name is rejected, the applicant may file a written reconsideration request with the Registrar of Corporations, Alberta Corporate Registry, within 30 days of the rejection notice. The request must include the original NUANS name search report, a statement of the distinctiveness of the proposed name, and any legal submissions showing compliance with the Alberta Business Corporations Act and Name Regulations. If the Registrar maintains the rejection, the applicant may appeal to the Court of King's Bench of Alberta for judicial review under the Administrative Procedures and Jurisdiction Act, RSA 2000, c A-1. There is no statutory extension of the name reservation window; a new name search and reservation filing will be required after the 90-day expiration.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted only if the registered office is a physical street address in Alberta capable of accepting legal service of process. Post office boxes are prohibited. For a low-risk MarTech/SEO SaaS company, a licensed virtual office with a physical Alberta street address, mail forwarding, and normal business-hours reception services is generally accepted by the Alberta Corporate Registry. The entity must retain access to all corporate records and financial books at or through the registered office to satisfy the Business Corporations Act and CRA compliance standards.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low: estimated annual probability of unannounced physical inspection is below 5% for a non-licensed, low-risk, software-as-a-service analytics entity without a high-risk AML profile. Inspections are typically triggered by CRA audit criteria, missing periodic filings, third-party complaints, or adverse AML reporting, not by routine registry activity.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act (Alberta), RSA 2000, c B-9, ss. 5(1), 6, 7(1), 8, 12, 17(1)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of Corporations, Service Alberta, Government of Alberta
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (Form 1) and Certificate of Incorporation issued by the Registrar
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital required under the ABCA. A company may commence business with one common share issued at nominal par value. No escrow account or paid-up capital deposit is mandatory for incorporation.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF [●] ALBERTA HOLDINGS INC. The incorporator, acting as the first board of directors, hereby resolves: (1) the corporate name of the Company is adopted as set forth in the Certificate of Incorporation; (2) the subscription of one (1) common share by [●] is accepted, and the share certificate shall be issued upon payment of nominal value; (3) the registered office of the Company is established at [●], Alberta, effective immediately; (4) [●] is appointed President, Secretary-Treasurer, and sole director until the first annual general meeting; and (5) the officers are authorized to open corporate bank accounts, execute contracts, and make necessary statutory filings.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry via authorized service provider or online at Service Alberta corporate registry portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a NUANS name search through an authorized Corporate Registry agent or online service. Ensure the proposed corporate name is distinguishable from existing names in Alberta and does not contravene Part 3 of the Business Corporations Act. If a numbered name is preferred, skip this step. If the name requires reservation, file a Name Reservation Request and pay the statutory fee.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is refused or distinguishable-conflict arises, choose a different name or switch to a numbered corporation; resubmit the name reservation or incorporate under a new name without penalty.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft Articles of Incorporation and Authorizing Consents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Incorporator and legal counsel / service provider
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the Articles of Incorporation (Form 1) containing the corporate name, share structure, registered office address within Alberta, authorized share capital, restrictions on share transfer (if any), number of directors (minimum one), and any permitted business restrictions. Secure signed Consents to Act as Director from each proposed director. Confirm that the registered office is a physical address in Alberta with mail delivery capability.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry identifies drafting omissions or incomplete information, revise the Articles to comply with ABCA mandatory wording and resubmit for processing; no additional penalty is incurred for corrected filings.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File Articles and Pay Government Fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry (electronic filing via authorized service provider)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the authenticated Articles of Incorporation and Consent to Act documentation through the Alberta Corporate Registry online portal. Pay the prescribed incorporation filing fee using a registry-approved payment method. Keep the transaction receipt for reference. Filing may be effected by a law firm, corporate registry agent, or directly through the registry's online filing service.
required_dossiers: Signed Articles of Incorporation in machine-readable format
NUANS Report or Name Reservation (for named companies)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried or rejected, review the deficiency summary and any registry remarks; promptly file an amended Articles package or supplement the missing consents. Use the Alberta Corporate Registry customer service escalation path to obtain a written explanation and cure timeline.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Certificate of Incorporation and Register Corporate Extract Data
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After registry approval, retrieve the electronic Certificate of Incorporation. Verify the legal name, registered office, directors, and incorporation date on the corporate extract. If the company intends to open a position under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, obtain the CRA business number in the next step.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Certificate contains facts that do not match the approved Articles, file a Notice of Change request with Service Alberta using Form 6 to correct the registry record; supported by an affidavit of correction.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors / Shareholders (by written resolution)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene an organizational board meeting or sign a unanimous written resolution. Adopt the company's bylaws regulating director meetings, officer duties, banking, borrowing, and share transfers. Submit certifications confirming that the registered office consent and officer appointment forms are in force. File any initial director appointment with the registry in the prescribed format.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the board resolution is internally inconsistent, amend the resolution by further board or shareholder resolution; re-file the director appointment record with Service Alberta within 15 days after any change.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register with Canada Revenue Agency for Tax Accounts
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) – Business Registration Online portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Using the Certificate of Incorporation and the CRA business number request, register for the federal corporate income tax account, GST/HST account (if taxable supplies exceed $30,000), payroll account (if hiring employees), and provincial programs. Complete the Alberta Corporate Tax Registration through CRA to obtain provincial corporate income tax account. Use the CRA BAS limiter if the company is a non-resident owner filer.
required_dossiers: Corporate Extract or registered office notice
CRA Form RC1 or Business Registration Online data
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CRA flags the registration, respond to CRA's online clarification request by providing the corporate extract and the intent-to-supply nexus explanation. Request reassessment if the CRA account is activated under a different legal entity.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable – no industrial licensing regime applies to a pure MarTech SEO analytics software company under ISIC 6201 / NAICS 541511.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not required – no sectoral operating license or manufacturing permit for SaaS data analytics tools in Alberta.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – no physical construction or industrial activity subject to the Alberta Environmental Protection and Enhancement Act; no EIA registration required for a software/SaaS business.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable at point-of-service; if a leased office is established, the tenant must comply with municipal wastewater regulations, Alberta Ambient Air Quality Objectives, and the Safe Drinking Water Act. Server and cloud footprint emissions are upstream and not subject to direct Alberta permitting.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Non-industrial workspace: obtain an occupancy permit under the Alberta Safety Codes Act (fire and structural safety sign-off) for leased offices. Maintain Alberta Occupational Health and Safety workplace compliance, including emergency planning, first aid kits, and incident reporting. No civil defense or fire safety license is specifically required for remote software operations.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) - Federal and Provincial Tax Authorities, portal at cra-arc.gc.ca
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Canadian corporations obtain Business Number (BN) upon incorporation via CRA online portal or Form RC1. Foreign entities register for Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) through CRA International Tax program or provincial process.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box elections available; Canadian corporations taxed at entity level. Hybrid mismatch rules apply under GAAR.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Real-time GST/HST reporting via CRA portal; API integration and digital clearance required for large registrants; electronic invoicing encouraged with digital stamps in applicable cases.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods exported or digital services supplied to non-residents qualify for 0% GST/HST rate upon proof of export or non-resident consumption.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA audits export claims; fraudulent claims attract penalties up to 200% of evaded tax, interest, and potential criminal sanctions with retrospective clawbacks.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada); foreign exchange and anti-money laundering supervision delegated to FINTRAC and OSFI (Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains a fully convertible currency regime with no exchange control legislation governing current or capital account transactions; the wartime Exchange Control Act was repealed in 1951. Capital and profit remittance are unrestricted, subject only to Part XIII withholding tax on payments to non-residents (dividends generally 25% statutory, reduced to 5%-15% under applicable tax treaties) and to PCMLTFA/FINTRAC reporting thresholds (C$10,000 cash or wire monitoring). For an Alberta SaaS exporter, subscription sales are current-account transactions and are freely remittable without approval. Dividends, intercompany loan repayments, and equity repatriation by non-resident shareholders encounter zero conversion friction; however, the paying bank will require a valid T106 information return for any cross-border related-party services and proof of beneficial ownership to apply treaty withholding relief.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Canada imposes no statutory surrender ratio or repatriation timeline on export proceeds; exporters may hold foreign currency indefinitely in USD or other external accounts. The only compliance requirements are: (1) FINTRAC reporting for receipts of C$10,000 or more; (2) Statistics Canada trade reporting on the Canadian International Merchandise Trade (CIMT) form — applicable only to merchandise, not to exported software services; and (3) GST/HST zero-rating documentation (exported supplies of intangible personal property to non-residents are zero-rated under ETA Schedule VI, Part V, Section 21, requiring the supplier to retain evidence of non-resident status of the client).

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: MEDIUM — permissible strictly as a supplementary corridor, not as a primary settlement account. Canadian licensing law does not confer deposit-taking or CDIC insurance status on foreign EMIs (Wise Business, Payoneer, Mercury, Brex); funds held at such institutions are uninsured corporate deposits and are not eligible for GST/HST credit offsets or payroll processing under the Canada Revenue Agency's individual-account matching rules. Legal constraints include: (1) PCMLTFA requires an annual report of any record keeping on currency transactions — EMIs may refuse to share beneficiary data with the primary Canadian bank; (2) the EMI cannot issue Canadian payee cheques or process E-pay Canada / ACSS direct debits; and (3) inbound wire originations from an EMI to a Canadian bank are frequently flagged for enhanced source-of-funds review. Recommended architecture: Big-6 Canadian CAD/USD accounts as the spine, plus a Wise Business or PayPal Business account as a dedicated receiving rail for Stripe/Paddle USD equivalents in jurisdictions with poor SWIFT connectivity.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote onboarding is permitted and is the standard for a newly incorporated Alberta Business Corporation. No federal or provincial statute mandates physical branch appearance; the federal Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA) and FINTRAC regulations allow banks to verify identity electronically through government-issued ID, biometric eKYC, and attestation by a qualified legal or accounting professional. In practice, the bank's compliance department will require: (1) an authenticated video interview with all authorized signatories (director or CFO) with a corporate officer; (2) notarized or certified true copies of passports and proof of residential address; (3) the Alberta Corporate Registry (Alberta Corporate Access / Corporate Registry) certificate of status and annual return extracts; and (4) a Persons with Significant Control (PSC) register declaration (mandatory under Canada Business Corporations Act and Alberta Business Corporations Act as amended in 2023). Physical presence at an Albertan branch is waived if the company engages an Alberta-licensed lawyer to certify the corporate documents and a video KYC interview is completed by the Treasury Director.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Newly incorporated shelf company with zero trading history and no tax registration (registered < 6 months; no Business Number / CRA account issued)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certificate of Incorporation from Alberta Corporate Registry; Registration Extract (Corporate Access) for the legal entity including registered office; CRA Business Number confirmation (RT 1-9 / CRA letter); 12-month cash-flow forecast; Customer-introducing letter from a Big-4 auditor or licensed Alberta law firm attesting to economic substance; rent agreement or commercial lease for the Alberta head office; business plan evidencing software-as-a-service recurring revenue model.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident beneficial owner or director resident in a high-risk or restricted jurisdiction (e.g., jurisdictions on FATF grey list or with insufficient AML controls)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified passport copies of all directors and PSC register; jurisdictional tax residency certificate (CRS-linked); independent AML risk rating from a recognized screening provider (Refinitiv World-Check); prior 6-month bank statement from a foreign regulated FIU bank; a written business and substance plan outlining Alberta staff hiring and local revenue generation; consent to video interview with bank's compliance officer in English or with a certified translator.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound capital injections sourced from cryptocurrency exchanges or from pre-revenue seed rounds with fragmented investor wire history
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed SAFE / share-subscription agreement with corporate minutes approving treasury inflow; investor-by-investor source-of-funds statements from regulated crypto exchanges (with withdrawal invoices); open-source chain-analysis report (crystal/Chainalysis) on the originating wallet; signed director declaration of source of investor capital (salary, inheritance, or asset sale — matching tax slips); where applicable, a formal seed-financing closing statement from the law firm.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Daily subscription revenue aggregated via Stripe/Paddle creates high payment-volume velocity ahead of corporate tax filings (revenue concentration in small FX micro-transactions)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Original merchant-of-record settlement reports from Stripe and Paddle (weekly payout records with client IP, email, and invoice numbers); read-only API access granted to the bank's forensic team for 12 months; copies of end-customer subscription invoices evidencing B2B or B2C SaaS; corporate income tax estimates filed with the CRA (T2 form) showing forecast revenues; annualized GTV threshold below C$1M to remain in the bank's low-risk standard parameter.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Outbound cross-border vendor payments with vague descriptor fields (e.g., 'services', 'consulting', 'infrastructure') resulting in financial-action-task-force (FATF) travel-rule breaches
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Vendor and supplier master file with full legal name and jurisdiction; executed master services agreement (MSA) with payment schedule; itemized invoices road-mapped to delivery milestones; cloud infrastructure order forms (AWS, DigitalOcean, Datadog) if processing-related; completed SWIFT MT103 with mandatory structured purpose code and a copy of ultimate beneficiary ownership declaration for related-party payees.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All inbound foreign capital must route via SWIFT (MT103) with an explicit instruction line; the bank will apply Treaty-based withholding assessment at source and will require proof of direct beneficial ownership (Form NR302 / relevant waiver). Authorized lanes: (1) Equity injection from the parent or non-resident investor — a share subscription, director resolution, and the SEDAR-free (private placement) exemption under Alberta securities laws; (2) Shareholder loan cross-border — an executed promissory note with arm's-length interest (Canada Revenue Agency prescribed rate quarterly), a T1134 information return if the foreign shareholder owns 25% or more of the corporation, and intercompany recharging accruals; (3) SaaS revenue settlement from Stripe/Paddle — a merchant settlement batch in EUR, GBP, USD, and CAD with an FX conversion invoice from the payment processor. The routing protocol for a USD receiving account at an Alberta Big-6 bank will use the Canadian bank's US intermediary (e.g., BMO's New York branch, RBC's RBC Bank in Georgia) and a final Lynx/ACSS same-day clearing for CAD conversion. No capital-controls approval or Central Bank permit is required; the ONLY formalities are: (a) record the receipts as current or capital inflows in the company's CRA F310/foreign source income schedule; (b) where cumulative inbound investment from non-residents is below the Investment Canada Act notification threshold (CAD 1.1 billion for WTO investors — nearly always applicable to an Alberta SaaS treasury), file the voluntary notification if total capitalization exceeds CAD 5 million; and (c) keep all MT103 originals, SWIFT credits, and KYC-flagged reversals for 7 years.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound Treasury rails are sequenced by value: (1) High-value vendor and intercompany payments: SWIFT MT103 over BMO Global Payments Plus or RBC's correspondent network with GPS tracking (recovered in 5–20 minutes via GPI); for CAD-denominated domestic payments, ACSS same-day cheque/direct debit or send-to-email Interac e-Transfer (under C$3,000); (2) Intraday and real-time transfers: Lynx RTGS / Ascend instant payment for intraday cash concentration across the Alberta entity and its Canada/US clinics; (3) Commercial letters of credit: not applicable — an SEO content analytics SaaS delivers intangible property (AI algorithms, crawl data, keyword reports) and does not trigger documentary trade instruments; all cross-border services settlement is on open account terms with respective confirmation invoices; (4) Recurring low-value international contractor payments: aggregator rails (Card via Visa/Mastercard corporate cards; Stripe Connect payouts; Payoneer/Wise) with a domestic ACSS sweep and monthly OFAC/PEP screening; (5) Export documentation: zero GST/HST charged under ETA zero-rating for exported SaaS; CRA requires a copy of the order form and proof of the non-resident identity of the buyer (IP address, billing address, corporate registry extract). For all outbound trade payments, the CFO must attach a purpose code per Canadian SWIFT National Purpose Code list — the most frequent are 'Software and SaaS license' for subscription feed purchases, 'Computer services, data processing' for dev-ops, and 'Management consulting' for external SEO specialists. The CAD account (Lynx/ACSS) must not operate with an overdraft for SWIFT outbound; the treasury must maintain a C$25,000 minimum buffer as a liquidity float for FX odd-lots.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: FX Spot (T+2) contracts — plain-vanilla USD/CAD and GBP/CAD conversions executed on the bank's electronic platform (BMO FX Online, RBC Vertex) without specialized documentation

Outright FX Forwards (deliverable) — fixed-date USD/CAD, EUR/CAD, GBP/CAD cover for committed SaaS enterprise contracts and capex liabilities; maturities up to 12 calendar months under a standard FX Master Agreement (ISDA-style) even with a C$1M notional

Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) — permitted where the foreign counterparty currency is non-deliverable (CNY, KRW, INR); the Canadian bank prices via its offshore book; the hedge must be documented under ISDA 1998 FX Definitions with a discrete PD mirroring the settled amount

Cross-Currency Swap (CAD/USD, legacy maturity extension) — permissible for intercompany loan hedging on multi-year bridge notes; executed under an ISDA Master Agreement and Credit Support Annex if the bank requires margin, though a Canadian mid-cap treasury is normally exempt from OSFI's uncleared margin rules below the C$750M aggregate notional threshold

FX SWAP / Roll-over swap — recurrence-hedging instrument for rolling forward an expiring forward position into the next tenor without altering the underlying exposure, permitted without regulatory swap-execution-facility (SEF) treatment for CAD/USD because the transaction settles on a traditional Canadian bank platform

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry (Service Alberta / Registrar of Companies)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the anniversary date of incorporation or continuation; repeats annually on the same anniversary rule and does not follow a fixed calendar-year deadline.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file by the deadline places the corporation in inactive registry status, prevents issuance of certificates of compliance, and continued default permits the Registrar to strike the corporation off the register after statutory notice.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: ABCA imposes no revenue or asset threshold for audit. An auditor must be appointed at each annual general meeting unless all shareholders entitled to vote unanimously consent to waive the auditor appointment for that fiscal year; the unanimous waiver is not available to reporting issuers.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS for publicly accountable/reporting enterprises; Canadian ASPE for private business corporations; both constitute acceptable GAAP under Alberta law.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Alberta requires no annual public UBO confirmation filing.
